title: Reaction rate and energy - 123 school
heading: Reaction rate and energy
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.q: What is an exothermic reaction?
questions.a: A reaction in which energy is released

questions.q: What is an endothermic reaction?
questions.a: A reaction in which energy is absorbed

questions.q: Is the combustion of natural gas exothermic or endothermic?
questions.a: Exothermic

questions.q: Is photosynthesis exothermic or endothermic?
questions.a: Endothermic (energy from sunlight is absorbed)

questions.q: What is the activation energy?
questions.a: The minimum energy needed to start a reaction

questions.q: What is a catalyst?
questions.a: A substance that speeds up a reaction and is not used up itself

questions.q: What does a catalyst do to the activation energy?
questions.a: It becomes lower

questions.q: What does a catalyst do to the heat of reaction?
questions.a: Nothing, the heat of reaction stays the same

questions.q: What is an effective collision?
questions.a: A collision between particles with enough energy and in the right orientation, after which they react

questions.q: Why does a reaction go faster at a higher temperature?
questions.a: The particles move faster, so there are more effective collisions per second

questions.q: Why does a reaction go faster at a higher concentration?
questions.a: There are more particles per volume, so more collisions per second

questions.q: Why does zinc powder react faster with hydrochloric acid than a piece of zinc of the same mass?
questions.a: Powder has a larger contact surface

questions.q: What happens to the reaction rate of gases if you increase the pressure?
questions.a: The rate becomes greater, because there are more particles per volume

questions.q: According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. What happens to the rate for a 20 °C rise?
questions.a: 4 times as great: 2 × 2 = 4

questions.q: According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 20 °C a reaction takes 80 s. How long does the reaction take at 40 °C?
questions.a: 20 s: 20 → 40 °C is doubling 2 times, the rate becomes 4 times as great, so 80 s : 4 = 20 s

questions.q: According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 50 °C a reaction takes 12 s. How long does the reaction take at 30 °C?
questions.a: 48 s: 50 → 30 °C is halving the rate 2 times, the rate becomes 4 times as small, so 12 s × 4 = 48 s

questions.q: According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 20 °C a reaction takes 100 s. How long does the reaction take at 30 °C?
questions.a: 50 s: the rate becomes 2 times as great, so 100 s : 2 = 50 s

questions.q: According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. How many times as great is the rate at 50 °C as at 20 °C?
questions.a: 8 times: a rise of 30 °C is doubling 3 times, 2 × 2 × 2 = 8

questions.q: According to the rule of thumb, the reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. At 60 °C a reaction takes 5 s. How long does the reaction take at 20 °C?
questions.a: 80 s: 60 → 20 °C is halving the rate 4 times, the rate becomes 16 times as small, so 5 s × 16 = 80 s

questions.q: How is the reaction rate defined?
questions.a: The change in concentration per time (Δc : Δt)

questions.q: What is a suitable unit for reaction rate?
questions.a: mol/(L·s)

questions.q: The concentration of substance A falls from 0.80 mol/L to 0.50 mol/L in 30 s. Calculate the average reaction rate.
In a reaction, 12 mL of gas is formed in 40 s. Calculate the average reaction rate in mL/s.
How do you make the reaction between magnesium and hydrochloric acid slower?
questions.a: Lower the temperature

questions.q: In an energy diagram of an exothermic reaction, where is the level of the products?
questions.a: Lower than the level of the reactants

questions.q: In an energy diagram of an endothermic reaction, where is the level of the products?
questions.a: Higher than the level of the reactants

questions.q: How do you read the heat of reaction from an energy diagram?
questions.a: The difference in height between the level of the reactants and that of the products

questions.q: In an energy diagram the reactants are at 120 kJ, the products at 80 kJ and the top of the hill at 150 kJ. What is the activation energy?
In an energy diagram the reactants are at 120 kJ, the products at 80 kJ and the top of the hill at 150 kJ. How much energy is released in the reaction?
The combustion of methane releases 8.9 × 10<sup>5</sup> J per mole of methane. How much energy is released in the combustion of 8.0 g of methane? (M = 16.04 g/mol)
The combustion of methane releases 8.9 × 10<sup>5</sup> J per mole of methane. How much energy is released in the combustion of 2.0 mol of methane?
What is a dynamic equilibrium?
questions.a: The forward reaction and the reverse reaction proceed at the same rate

questions.q: What happens to the reaction rate while the reactants are being used up?
questions.a: The rate becomes smaller

questions.q: Give two ways to speed up a reaction.
questions.a: For example raise the temperature, raise the concentration, use a finer division of a solid or add a catalyst

questions.q: Explain why a catalyst makes a reaction faster.
questions.a: A catalyst lowers the activation energy, so more collisions have enough energy to react
